correctness.rationale: For m,n>=5 and G=C_m □ C_n, the ordinary 3-cut Alexander dual Y contains all N=mn vertices, all C(N,2) edges, precisely 6N triangles (induced length-two paths), and N square tetrahedra, with no 5-vertex faces since each five-set all whose triples are paths would satisfy 3|E|=20. Straight-path free edge/triangle collapses, square tetrahedron/corner-triangle and diagonal/corner-triangle collapses yield a 2D torus cellulation with N(N-13)/2 extra one-cells, so H_2(Y)=Q and H_1(Y)=Q^B with B=N(N-13)/2+2. Translations preserve the oriented torus fundamental class. Only nonzero order-two translations setwise stabilize edges in the complete 1-skeleton, giving signed chain trace -N/2, all nonidentity elements fix no vertices/triangles/tetrahedra. Hopf trace yields H1 character B at identity, 2-N/2 at order 2, 2 otherwise. Equivariant Alexander duality twists by the permutation sign σ(t)=(-1)^{a n(m-1)+b m(n-1)}, determining homology degrees N-5,N-4 and all character averages. Independent code enumerated 5×5 Y f-vector (25,300,150,25), mod-two boundary ranks (24,124,25), Betti dimensions (152,1), and all translation traces; finite arithmetic supports the uniform collapse proof.

originality.rationale: The Bayer–Denker–Jelić Milutinović–Sundaram–Xue sequel studies ordinary cut complexes of rectangular PATH grids P_m□P_n (including 3-cut Betti counts) and dihedral actions of individual cycles. Their exact theorems do not extend by simple substitution to periodic two-cycle products with torus H_2 and all translations. The strongest closely named published torus result uses TOTAL two-cut complexes with a 1D graph Alexander dual, not ordinary three-cut with 3D square tetrahedra. Prior nonequivariant toroidal homology does not recover these oriented characters or the same/opposite parity quotient criterion. No covering prior full T-character was found, with unindexed equivariant-topology risk.

value.rationale: The ordinary toroidal three-cut complex is a natural periodic counterpart of cut complexes on rectangular path grids. The complete T-representation and subgroup quotient homology, especially survival of the top class iff both cycle lengths have equal parity, are motivated symmetry data hidden by ordinary Betti numbers. The two-dimensional torus fundamental class and ground-set Alexander-duality sign explain a genuine parity phenomenon beyond an arbitrary finite computation.

limitations: Ordinary Δ3 not total-cut, m,n>=5; geometric quotient |X|/H distinct from cut complex of graph quotient.
Only translation group, not reflections/coordinate swaps; all homology claims over Q.
